title: Steal Steve Jobs' Secret Weapon: Analogy Stacking
summary: Steve Jobs used powerful analogies to sell products by appealing to emotion rather than just logical facts. The creator explains that analogy stacking creates a world within a world until logic steps aside and imagination takes over. Princeton neuroscientists have shown that this kind of communication creates matching brain activity between the speaker and the listener.
key_points: Steve Jobs used analogies like calling a computer 'a bicycle of the mind' in the 1990s and calling PCs 'trucks' in 2010 to make computers the exception and sell iPads.
Analogy stacking means building a world, then a world inside that world, making listeners follow deeper until logic steps aside and imagination takes the wheel.
Most experts speak to the filing cabinet in the head using facts, features, and numbers, but analogies target feelings and move you from a cognitive speaker to an emotional speaker.
Princeton neuroscientists scanned speakers and listeners and found that when communication lands successfully, the listener's brain activity mirrors the speaker's brain.
To use this technique, first find an analogy for your business, and second, stack it and repeat it often.
